g.text: N1 [Context]
MLPs are foundational deep-learning blocks
Multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) [1, 2, 3], also known as fully-connected
feedforward neural networks, are foundational building blocks of today's
deep learning models.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=3) Multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) [1, 2, 3], also known as fully-connected feedforward neural networks, are foundational building blocks of today's deep learning models.

g.text: N2 [Context]
MLPs justified by universal approximation theorem
The importance of MLPs can never be overstated, since they are the default
models in machine learning for approximating nonlinear functions, due to
their expressive power guaranteed by the universal approximation theorem
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=1) The importance of MLPs can never be overstated, since they are the default models in machine learning for approximating nonlinear functions, due to their expressive power guaranteed by the universal approximation theorem [3].

g.text: N3 [Context]
MLPs have significant drawbacks
However, are MLPs the best nonlinear regressors we can build? Despite the
prevalent use of MLPs, they have significant drawbacks.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) However, are MLPs the best nonlinear regressors we can build? Despite the prevalent use of MLPs, they have significant drawbacks.

g.text: N4 [Context]
MLPs: heavy parameters, low interpretability
In transformers [4] for example, MLPs consume almost all non-embedding
parameters and are typically less interpretable (relative to attention
layers) without post-analysis tools [5].
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=2) In transformers [4] for example, MLPs consume almost all non-embedding parameters and are typically less interpretable (relative to attention layers) without post-analysis tools [5].

g.text: N5 [Method]
Propose KANs as MLP alternative
We propose a promising alternative to MLPs, called
Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs).
g.title: N5 [Method] (cites=0) We propose a promising alternative to MLPs, called Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs).

g.text: N6 [Method]
KANs inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem
Whereas MLPs are inspired by the universal approximation theorem, KANs are
inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem [6, 7, 8].
g.title: N6 [Method] (cites=3) Whereas MLPs are inspired by the universal approximation theorem, KANs are inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem [6, 7, 8].

g.text: N7 [Method]
Learnable activations on edges, not nodes
Like MLPs, KANs have fully-connected structures. However, while MLPs place
fixed activation functions on nodes (“neurons”), KANs place learnable
activation functions on edges (“weights”), as illustrated in Figure 0.1.
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) Like MLPs, KANs have fully-connected structures. However, while MLPs place fixed activation functions on nodes (“neurons”), KANs place learnable activation functions on edges (“weights”), as illustrated in Figure 0.1.

g.text: N8 [Method]
Each weight is a learnable 1D spline
As a result, KANs have no linear weight matrices at all: instead, each
weight parameter is replaced by a learnable 1D function parametrized as a
spline.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) As a result, KANs have no linear weight matrices at all: instead, each weight parameter is replaced by a learnable 1D function parametrized as a spline.

g.text: N9 [Method]
Nodes only sum incoming signals
KANs' nodes simply sum incoming signals without applying any
non-linearities.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) KANs' nodes simply sum incoming signals without applying any non-linearities.

g.text: N10 [Result]
KANs use smaller computation graphs
One might worry that KANs are hopelessly expensive, since each
MLP's weight parameter becomes KAN's spline function. Fortunately,
KANs usually allow much smaller computation graphs than MLPs.
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=0) One might worry that KANs are hopelessly expensive, since each MLP's weight parameter becomes KAN's spline function. Fortunately, KANs usually allow much smaller computation graphs than MLPs.

g.text: N11 [Prior_Work]
Prior KA-inspired networks exist
Unsurprisingly, the possibility of using
Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem to build
neural networks has been studied [9, 10, 11, 12, 13,
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=8) Unsurprisingly, the possibility of using Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem to build neural networks has been studied [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16].

g.text: N12 [Limitation]
Prior work stuck at depth-2 width-(2n+1)
However, most work has stuck with the original depth-2 width-(2n +
1) representation, and many did not have the chance to leverage
more modern techniques (e.g., back propagation) to train the
networks.
g.title: N12 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, most work has stuck with the original depth-2 width-(2n + 1) representation, and many did not have the chance to leverage more modern techniques (e.g., back propagation) to train the networks.

g.text: N13 [Prior_Work]
[12]: depth-2 KA breaks COD on compositional
structure
In [12], a depth-2 width-(2n + 1) representation was
investigated, with breaking of the curse of
dimensionality observed both empirically and with an
approximation theory given compositional structures of…
g.title: N13 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) In [12], a depth-2 width-(2n + 1) representation was investigated, with breaking of the curse of dimensionality observed both empirically and with an approximation theory given compositional structures of the function.

g.text: N14 [Contribution]
Generalize KA to arbitrary width/depth; AI+Science
Our contribution lies in generalizing the original
Kolmogorov-Arnold representation to arbitrary widths and depths,
revitalizing and contextualizing it in today's deep learning
world, as well as using extensive empirical experiments to…
g.title: N14 [Contribution] (cites=0) Our contribution lies in generalizing the original Kolmogorov-Arnold representation to arbitrary widths and depths, revitalizing and contextualizing it in today's deep learning world, as well as using extensive empirical experiments to highlight its potential for AI + Science due to its accuracy and interpretability.

g.text: N15 [Method]
KANs combine splines + MLPs
Despite their elegant mathematical interpretation, KANs are nothing more
than combinations of splines and MLPs, leveraging their respective strengths
and avoiding their respective weaknesses.
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Despite their elegant mathematical interpretation, KANs are nothing more than combinations of splines and MLPs, leveraging their respective strengths and avoiding their respective weaknesses.

g.text: N16 [Prior_Work]
Splines: accurate, local, multi-resolution
Splines are accurate for low-dimensional functions,
easy to adjust locally, and able to switch between
different resolutions.
g.title: N16 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Splines are accurate for low-dimensional functions, easy to adjust locally, and able to switch between different resolutions.

g.text: N17 [Limitation]
Splines suffer curse of dimensionality
However, splines have a serious curse of dimensionality (COD)
problem, because of their inability to exploit compositional
structures.
g.title: N17 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, splines have a serious curse of dimensionality (COD) problem, because of their inability to exploit compositional structures.

g.text: N18 [Prior_Work]
MLPs: feature learning yes, univariate no
MLPs, on the other hand, suffer less from COD thanks to
their feature learning, but are less accurate than
splines in low dimensions, because of their inability
to optimize univariate functions.
g.title: N18 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) MLPs, on the other hand, suffer less from COD thanks to their feature learning, but are less accurate than splines in low dimensions, because of their inability to optimize univariate functions.

g.text: N18b [Prior_Work]
ReLU-k MLPs ~ splines link established
The link between MLPs using ReLU-k as activation functions and splines have
been established in [17, 18].
g.title: N18b [Prior_Work] (cites=2) The link between MLPs using ReLU-k as activation functions and splines have been established in [17, 18].

g.text: N19 [Method]
KANs: MLP outside, spline inside
To learn a function accurately, a model should not only learn the
compositional structure (external degrees of freedom), but should
also approximate well the univariate functions (internal degrees
of freedom). KANs are such models since…
g.title: N19 [Method] (cites=0) To learn a function accurately, a model should not only learn the compositional structure (external degrees of freedom), but should also approximate well the univariate functions (internal degrees of freedom). KANs are such models since they have MLPs on the outside and splines on the inside.

g.text: N20 [Result]
KANs learn features and optimize accurately
As a result, KANs can not only learn features (thanks to their
external similarity to MLPs), but can also optimize these learned
features to great accuracy (thanks to their internal similarity to
splines).
g.title: N20 [Result] (cites=0) As a result, KANs can not only learn features (thanks to their external similarity to MLPs), but can also optimize these learned features to great accuracy (thanks to their internal similarity to splines).

g.text: N20a [Method]
Worked example: f = exp(∑ sin² xi)/N
For example, given a high dimensional function f(x1, ..., xN) =
g.title: N20a [Method] (cites=0) For example, given a high dimensional function f(x1, ..., xN) = exp(1/N ∑ sin^2(xi)), (1.1)

g.text: N20b [Limitation]
Splines fail at large N (COD)
splines would fail for large N due to COD;
g.title: N20b [Limitation] (cites=0) splines would fail for large N due to COD;

g.text: N20c [Limitation]
MLPs inefficient on exp/sin with ReLU
MLPs can potentially learn the the generalized additive structure, but they
are very inefficient for approximating the exponential and sine functions
with say, ReLU activations.
g.title: N20c [Limitation] (cites=0) MLPs can potentially learn the the generalized additive structure, but they are very inefficient for approximating the exponential and sine functions with say, ReLU activations.

g.text: N21 [Result]
KANs outperform MLPs by large margin
In contrast, KANs can learn both the compositional structure and
the univariate functions quite well, hence outperforming MLPs by a
large margin (see Figure 3.1).
g.title: N21 [Result] (cites=0) In contrast, KANs can learn both the compositional structure and the univariate functions quite well, hence outperforming MLPs by a large margin (see Figure 3.1).

g.text: P21 [Proof]
Fig. 3.1: KANs vs MLPs
see Figure 3.1
g.title: P21 [Proof] (cites=0) see Figure 3.1

g.text: N22 [Contribution]
KANs improve accuracy + interpretability over MLPs
Throughout this paper, we will use extensive numerical experiments
to show that KANs can lead to accuracy and interpretability
improvement over MLPs, at least on small-scale AI + Science tasks.
g.title: N22 [Contribution] (cites=0) Throughout this paper, we will use extensive numerical experiments to show that KANs can lead to accuracy and interpretability improvement over MLPs, at least on small-scale AI + Science tasks.
